acceptance_evidence: At least one fresh Codex reference and at least two fresh Claude candidate runs use equivalent Applications4Life snapshots, the same Workbench prompt, pinned model/effort settings, and complete transcripts and runtime metrics.

Claude meets or exceeds Codex on factual/causal correctness, evidence calibration, coverage/actionability, Workbench fidelity, clarity, and weighted total, with every substantive dimension at least 4.0.

Claude's median usage is no more than 150,000 tokens and 1,500 seconds, with no Workbench schema failure, stale/deployed provenance error, unregistered correction, legacy/Ralph hook, or premature ranking before environment disposition.
Representative sample-codebase regression tasks confirm the hooks remain scoped, one-shot, fail-open for malformed input, and do not degrade ordinary implementation behavior.

The winning canonical prompt and hooks are installed globally, their hashes match the evaluated candidate, legacy registrations are removed, and a fresh Claude session reproduces the passing behavior.
assumptions: The user's explicit instruction authorizes repeated subscription-backed Claude and Codex runs and mutation of the user's global Claude prompt, hooks, settings, and installed claude-rigor harness.
The named Applications4Life task is diagnostic and read-only; scored runs may create only disposable Workbench records in isolated copies.
Provider throttling, authentication expiry, or outage is an external impasse only after bounded retries and preserved resumable evidence.

constraints: Preserve unrelated changes in both repositories and do not modify Applications4Life application code; use disposable copies or worktrees for scored trials.
Do not inspect secret-bearing paths prohibited by the Applications4Life AGENTS.md and redact any captured evidence.
Use the frozen rubric and Codex baseline; do not tune grading after seeing candidate results.

Preserve personal Graphify instructions and unrelated Claude settings; keep timestamped rollback backups.

desired_outcome: Claude Code, using the installed global prompt and hooks, meets or exceeds the established Codex baseline on every substantive grading dimension for the Applications4Life Workbench diagnosis prompt, remains within the 150,000-token and 25-minute ceilings, and preserves that behavior across representative disposable sample codebases; otherwise the campaign stops only at a reproducible provider or technical impasse.

facts.statement: The prior Claude v3 transcript did not meet the Codex comparison bar and showed premature investigation, duplicated legacy hooks, source-provenance errors, Workbench schema repair loops, and excessive cost.

The current global Claude configuration still registers the legacy Python completion guard and separate Workbench diagnosis hook instead of the planned self-contained claude-rigor preflight and sole Stop review.
The repository contains a locally verified resumable optimizer, a frozen rubric, the prior Claude and Codex transcripts, and a canonical claude-rigor prompt and hook source.

rationale: A locally verified optimization controller and a detailed v3 remediation plan exist, but the requested outcome requires live Claude and Codex trials, iterative prompt and hook changes, global installation, fresh-session verification, and measured parity on the named brownfield Workbench task.

assumptions: Claude and Codex CLIs remain authenticated and provider quota is available.
recommendation.choice: Execute a frozen-rubric champion-challenger campaign and deploy the best passing Claude prompt-and-hook bundle.
recommendation.rationale: This directly measures the named failure, protects against prompt overfitting with sample tasks and repetitions, and makes global promotion reversible and evidence-bound.
